name: Suriel
title: The angel mentioned in apocryphal tradition
summary: Suriel is an angel mentioned in Jewish apocryphal and pseudepigraphical literature, particularly in the Book of Enoch. He is counted among the archangels in certain traditions and is associated with the protection and guidance of souls. Suriel is not directly named by name in the canonical biblical scriptures but is part of the broader Jewish angelology from the intertestamental period.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Book of Enoch
keyEvents.description: Suriel is mentioned as one of the holy angels in 1 Enoch, where he is described as the angel over spirits and souls. Although this is not a canonical text, it provides background for Jewish angelology.

keyEvents.title: The role of angels in biblical tradition
keyEvents.description: Although Suriel is not named by name in the canon, biblical texts reflect a rich tradition of angels as God's messengers and servants.

keyEvents.title: The hierarchy of angels in Jewish tradition
keyEvents.description: Daniel mentions heavenly beings and archangels, a tradition to which Suriel belongs in broader Jewish literature.

keyEvents.title: The Protection of Angels over Humans
keyEvents.description: The Book of Psalms testifies to angels as protectors, a role also attributed to Suriel in extrabiblical texts.

keyEvents.title: Heavenly Beings Around God's Throne
keyEvents.description: Isaiah describes seraphim and heavenly beings who worship God, reflecting the angelic tradition to which Suriel belongs.
